cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 14,641 male physicians in the United States initially aged 50 years or older, including 1307 men with a history of prior cancer at randomization, were enrolled.
reason: The trial reports incident prostate cancer as an overall endpoint but does not report an aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, high-risk, or lethal prostate cancer incidence analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was also no significant effect of vitamin C on total cancer (active and placebo vitamin C groups, 17.6 and 17.5 events per 1000 person-years; HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.92-1.10; P = .86) or prostate cancer (active and placebo vitamin C groups, 9.4 and 9.2 cases per 1000 person-years; HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.90-1.15; P = .80).
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin C estimate is explicitly for overall incident prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Compared with placebo, vitamin E had no effect on the incidence of prostate cancer (active and placebo vitamin E groups, 9.1 and 9.5 events per 1000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR], 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85-1.09; P = .58) or total cancer (active and placebo vitamin E groups, 17.8 and 17.3 cases per 1000 person-years; HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.95-1.13; P = .41).
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin E estimate is explicitly for overall incident prostate cancer.
